mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.2%) compresses discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through lower equity valuation costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.5% signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 5-day returns due to reduced consumer spending capacity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates contractionary demand and supply shocks, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both GDPC1 and INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, CPIAUCSL exceeding 240 signals inflationary pressures that trigger negative S&P 500 20-day returns through reduced real equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 240 during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 indicates manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent low housing starts (HOUST ≤ 1000) reflect weak consumer demand, generating negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns through reduced retail and construction sector activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST ≤ 1000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) signals deteriorating consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 60-day returns via suppressed retail and housing market activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment phases (UNRATE > 6%), labor market stress suppresses consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns through reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6%.
